source_license: Public — official government data. Verify terms of use with Loudoun County before commercial redistribution.
ordinance_version: 2023 Zoning Ordinance rewrite (confirmed live via GIS service sample record: ZO_ORDINANCE="2023") — see Municode for full current text
pilot_notes: Loudoun County is the most important pilot jurisdiction. The Ashburn/Sterling area (Data Center Alley) is the largest data center market in the world by capacity. The county has a defined 'Data Center Facility' use and a Data Center Overlay District (DCOD). Zoning polygon geometry is real and live (1,271 features, live-verified 2026-08-13). Dimensional standards and most use classifications in this file are still drawn from general public knowledge about Loudoun County zoning and require official verification against the current (2023-rewrite) ordinance -- only 3 of the 58 real district codes the live geometry returns (PD-IP, AR1, JLMA-3) have an actual data-center permitted-use determination; see validation_report.json for the full breakdown.
known_limitations: Only 3 of 58 real live district codes have a researched data-center permitted-use determination -- the other 55 are unresearched, never 'prohibited'.

Three of the seven researched district codes in districts.json (I1, I2, B2) are pre-2023-ordinance-rewrite codes with no match among the live service's current codes -- they never resolve on a real parcel today.
Dimensional standards are approximate and require official verification against the current Loudoun County Zoning Ordinance.
Loudoun County has been revising its Zoning Ordinance — confirm which version is currently effective at https://www.loudoun.gov/zoning before relying on specific section numbers.

PD-IP (Planned Development - Industrial Park) development standards are largely governed by approved development plans and proffered conditions, which vary by parcel. Base ordinance standards are minimums only.

The Data Center Overlay District (DCOD) boundary requires official verification and is not yet wired into the pipeline as a real overlay layer — contact the Loudoun County Department of Planning and Zoning.

Parcel-level zoning_code is not published by Loudoun's parcel service -- connecting a parcel to this geometry requires a parcel-to-zoning spatial join, which does not exist in this codebase yet (planned, not yet built).
Use table completeness is partial — only 7 of 58 real district codes have any researched name/category, and only 3 have data-center-specific research.
notes: Pilot jurisdiction — Phase 1 of zoning intelligence system. Zoning polygon geometry moved from demo to live and verified 2026-08-13. Demonstrates complete architecture: jurisdiction config, district records, dimensional standards, use classifications, overlay data, source tracking, and confidence levels; district-level data-center research coverage remains the primary gap.
